meta.move: Long messages with curly quotes and a concession
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have until 4:40, Hale, so let's not waste it. Owen found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided on that zero, and when?

I want to be fair to Owen. I compared the essay with his in-class writing from September 24: 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices throughout, no quotations. This essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line, and none of those errors.

A forty-minute piece in September against an essay he wrote over a weekend, and you call that a comparison? Show me the September 24 piece; I'll read it myself. And you still haven't told me whether anyone spoke to Owen before that zero went in.
You’re right that the checker alone proves nothing. I’m taking it off the table. I’m relying on the writing and the version history.
Okay, I'm writing down that the checker is off the table. What version history, Hale, and what exactly does it show? Turn the screen so I can read it.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed, though you said in our meeting that the checker result is no longer part of your case. I still demand that the zero be withdrawn, and I want to read the September 24 writing and the version history myself. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: opening position, still demanding the zero be withdrawn, and she agreed to nothing.
What moved her: "I’m taking it off the table", because dropping the detector score removed her strongest attack and earned a flat okay and a real question about the version history.
What cost ground: nothing, though leaving her question about whether Owen was heard before the zero unanswered kept her in her opening position.
Try next time: in your first line, own that the zero went into the gradebook before anyone called her, then put the September 24 writing and the version history on screen so she can read the dates herself.
